title: Academor SAT Practice Test 8 Reading and Writing

questions.question:
The startup's first product was ____________: within a year, it was used in more than half of the city's restaurants, and competitors rushed to copy it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: ubiquitous
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Being used almost everywhere in the city makes the product ubiquitous.

questions.question:
The professor's comments on student essays were ____________ but kind: she pointed out every weak argument while also suggesting how each could be improved.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: rigorous
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Pointing out every weak argument is thorough and demanding, or rigorous; “but kind” adds the helpful suggestions.

questions.question:
Because the instructions were written in a technical style that few people could follow, the company hired a writer to ____________ them for ordinary users.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: simplify
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Instructions that are too technical need to be made easier, or simplified.

questions.question:
The historian argues that the king's reputation for cruelty is ____________, based largely on accounts written by his enemies long after his death.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: unwarranted
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

A reputation based mainly on hostile, late accounts is not justified: it is unwarranted.

questions.question:
Velcro was invented after a walk in the woods. In 1941 the Swiss engineer George de Mestral noticed that burrs from burdock plants clung stubbornly to his clothing and to his dog's fur, and when he examined them under a microscope, he saw that they were covered with tiny hooks. He spent years developing a fastener that copied this design.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the observation that led to the invention mentioned in the first sentence.
It explains why burdock plants grow in forests.
It describes a problem with Velcro that de Mestral later solved.
It compares Velcro with other kinds of fasteners.
questions.correct: It describes the observation that led to the invention mentioned in the first sentence.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The burrs and their hooks are the observation that inspired the invention.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Priya is waiting for the results of a science competition.

The judges had been in the other room for forty minutes. Priya had checked her watch so often that her friend Lena finally took it off her wrist and put it in her own pocket. “It doesn't make them go faster,” Lena said. Priya laughed, then went back to watching the door, counting the tiles on the floor between herself and it. There were thirty-one. There had been thirty-one the last four times, too.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To portray a character's nervousness as she waits for an important result
To explain how a character won a science competition
To describe an argument between two friends
To show that a character is bored by a long event
questions.correct: To portray a character's nervousness as she waits for an important result
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Checking her watch and counting the same tiles again and again show Priya's nerves.

questions.question:
Text 1

Some nutrition scientists have recommended that people avoid eating late at night, arguing that food eaten in the evening is more likely to be stored as fat than the same food eaten earlier in the day.

Text 2

Researcher Felipe Rojas compared two groups who ate the same total amount of food each day for eight weeks. One group ate most of its food before 3:00 p.m., and the other ate most of it after 6:00 p.m. The groups' weight changed by similar amounts, though the late eaters reported sleeping less well. Rojas concludes that the timing of meals may matter more for sleep than for weight.

Based on the texts, how would Rojas (Text 2) most likely respond to the scientists' argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that food eaten in the evening is more likely to be stored as fat
By suggesting that his results do not support the claim that late eating causes weight gain
By recommending that people eat most of their food after 6:00 p.m.
By claiming that the total amount of food people eat does not affect weight
questions.correct: By suggesting that his results do not support the claim that late eating causes weight gain
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Rojas found similar weight changes regardless of timing, which does not support the scientists' claim.

questions.question:
When the Mars rover Opportunity landed in 2004, it was expected to operate for only about 90 days. Instead, it kept exploring for more than fourteen years. Engineers credit several factors: winds on Mars periodically blew dust off its solar panels, restoring power, and the team on Earth learned to park the rover on slopes facing the Sun during the Martian winter.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The rover Opportunity stopped working after about 90 days.
Winds on Mars damaged the rover's solar panels.
The rover was designed to operate for fourteen years.
The rover Opportunity far outlasted its expected lifespan, thanks to both lucky conditions and careful planning.
questions.correct: The rover Opportunity far outlasted its expected lifespan, thanks to both lucky conditions and careful planning.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The text contrasts the expected 90 days with fourteen years and explains why.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Old Mr. Tanaka has tended the same garden for fifty years.

His granddaughter wanted to replace the crooked plum tree. It leaned toward the fence, she said, and its fruit was small and sour. Mr. Tanaka did not argue. Instead, he led her to the trunk and showed her the scar where her mother, at seven, had carved her initials, and the branch where her grandmother had hung a lantern every summer. The granddaughter was quiet for a while. Then she asked how to make the sour plums into jam.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Mr. Tanaka agrees that the plum tree should be replaced.
Mr. Tanaka's granddaughter decides to plant a new garden.
By sharing the tree's family history, Mr. Tanaka changes his granddaughter's view of it.
Mr. Tanaka is angry with his granddaughter for criticizing the tree.
questions.correct: By sharing the tree's family history, Mr. Tanaka changes his granddaughter's view of it.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

After learning the tree's history, the granddaughter wants to use its fruit instead of removing it.

questions.question:
Psychologist Ana Costa claims that people are more likely to finish a long online course if they regularly see how much progress they have made.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' claim?
options: Students in an online course who were shown a progress bar after each lesson completed the course more often than students in the same course who were not shown one.
Most students who signed up for online courses were working adults.
Students who finished the course rated it highly.
The online course included both video lessons and quizzes.
questions.correct: Students in an online course who were shown a progress bar after each lesson completed the course more often than students in the same course who were not shown one.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Showing progress led to more completions, directly supporting Costa's claim.

questions.question:
A school tested ways of encouraging students to eat vegetables at lunch. Staff concluded that serving vegetables before the rest of the meal had a larger effect than giving them appealing names on the menu, though combining the two worked best: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: students ate 32% of vegetables served on the side.
students ate 47% of vegetables served first and 41% of vegetables named on the menu, compared with 58% when both approaches were used.
students ate 41% of vegetables served first and 47% of vegetables named on the menu.
students ate 58% of vegetables named on the menu.
questions.correct: students ate 47% of vegetables served first and 41% of vegetables named on the menu, compared with 58% when both approaches were used.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only this choice compares the two approaches correctly and shows the combination did best.

questions.question:
Conservationists installed nest boxes for barn owls in Hollin Valley in 2012. They argue that the boxes helped the owls, noting that the number of nesting pairs ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: fell from about 14 to about 12 between 2006 and 2009.
stayed between about 12 and 14 before 2012 but rose to about 44 by 2021.
rose every year shown from 2006 to 2021.
questions.correct: stayed between about 12 and 14 before 2012 but rose to about 44 by 2021.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

A flat count before the boxes and a steady rise afterward supports the conservationists' argument.

questions.question:
Engineers tested whether recycled glass could replace some of the sand in concrete. They concluded that small amounts of glass had little effect on strength but that large amounts weakened the concrete: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: the standard mixture contained no recycled glass.
mixtures with 10% and 20% glass had strengths of 33 and 31 megapascals, close to the standard's 32, while the mixture with 40% glass had a strength of only 24.
the mixture with 10% glass was the strongest of the four mixtures.
every mixture containing glass was weaker than the standard mixture.
questions.correct: mixtures with 10% and 20% glass had strengths of 33 and 31 megapascals, close to the standard's 32, while the mixture with 40% glass had a strength of only 24.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only this choice shows both parts of the conclusion; the last choice is inaccurate.

questions.question:
Many tree species produce huge seed crops in some years and almost none in others, a pattern called masting. Ecologist Rhys Morgan found that in a forest of oaks, mice that eat acorns became very numerous after a mast year but then declined sharply in the following lean years. In mast years, so many acorns were produced that the mice could not eat them all, and many sprouted. These findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: masting may help oaks reproduce by producing more seeds than seed-eating animals can consume.
oaks produce more acorns when mice are numerous.
mice prefer acorns to all other foods.
acorns sprout only in years when no mice are present.
questions.correct: masting may help oaks reproduce by producing more seeds than seed-eating animals can consume.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

In mast years more acorns survive and sprout because the mice cannot eat them all.

questions.question:
Each of the paintings in the exhibit ____________ accompanied by a short recording in which the artist describes how it was made.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: is
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The subject is the singular “each,” so the verb is is.

questions.question:
The bakery opens at 6:00 a.m. on ____________ on weekends it opens at 8:00 a.m.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: weekdays;
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Two independent clauses are joined with a semicolon.

questions.question:
The city's population grew rapidly in the 1950s, and by 1960 it ____________ nearly doubled.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: had
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The doubling was completed by a past time (1960), so the past perfect had doubled is needed.

questions.question:
The mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan, who had little formal training in ____________ produced thousands of results, many of which are still being studied today.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: mathematics,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The nonessential clause “who had little formal training in mathematics” must be closed with a comma.

questions.question:
The museum offers guided tours in five languages, ____________ visitors from many countries to enjoy the exhibits.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: allowing
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The participle phrase “allowing visitors …” correctly describes the result of the first clause; the other choices create errors.

questions.question:
The garden has two sections: one for vegetables and one for ____________ each section is cared for by a different group of volunteers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: flowers.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A period ends the first sentence; a comma would create a comma splice.

questions.question:
Of all the planets in the solar system, Jupiter has the ____________ number of known moons; only Saturn has more.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: second-largest
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Ranking among many planets calls for the superlative “largest,” here “second-largest.”

questions.question:
Penguins cannot fly. ____________ they are excellent swimmers, using their wings like flippers to move quickly through the water.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: However,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Swimming well contrasts with being unable to fly.

questions.question:
The council approved the new park in March. ____________ construction began in June and was finished before the end of the year.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: Subsequently,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Construction followed the approval in time.

questions.question:
Some languages have no word for “blue” and use the same word for blue and green. ____________ some languages have two separate words for light blue and dark blue.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: Conversely,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Having two words for blue is the opposite of having none.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.
  • Between about 11,000 and 5,000 years ago, much of it was covered by grasslands and lakes.
  • Rock art from that period shows giraffes, elephants, and cattle.
  • Changes in Earth's orbit are thought to have shifted rainfall patterns and dried the region.

The student wants to emphasize how much the Sahara has changed.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.
Rock art in the Sahara shows giraffes, elephants, and cattle.
Although the Sahara is now the world's largest hot desert, between about 11,000 and 5,000 years ago much of it was covered by grasslands and lakes.
Changes in Earth's orbit are thought to have shifted rainfall patterns.
questions.correct: Although the Sahara is now the world's largest hot desert, between about 11,000 and 5,000 years ago much of it was covered by grasslands and lakes.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice contrasts the Sahara's past and present.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Hummingbirds have the highest metabolism of any bird.
  • Their hearts can beat more than 1,000 times per minute while they fly.
  • At night, many hummingbirds enter a state called torpor.
  • During torpor, their heart rate and body temperature drop sharply, saving energy.

The student wants to explain how hummingbirds save energy.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Hummingbirds have the highest metabolism of any bird.
At night, many hummingbirds save energy by entering torpor, during which their heart rate and body temperature drop sharply.
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times per minute while it flies.
Many hummingbirds enter a state called torpor.
questions.correct: At night, many hummingbirds save energy by entering torpor, during which their heart rate and body temperature drop sharply.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only this choice explains how torpor saves energy.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Ida B. Wells was an American journalist born in 1862.
  • In the 1890s she investigated and reported on lynchings in the southern United States.
  • She gathered evidence from newspapers, eyewitnesses, and public records.
  • In 2020 she was awarded a posthumous Pulitzer Prize special citation.

The student wants to emphasize the methods Wells used in her reporting.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In reporting on lynchings in the 1890s, Ida B. Wells gathered evidence from newspapers, eyewitnesses, and public records.
Ida B. Wells was an American journalist born in 1862.
In 2020 Ida B. Wells was awarded a posthumous Pulitzer Prize special citation.
In the 1890s Ida B. Wells reported on lynchings in the southern United States.
questions.correct: In reporting on lynchings in the 1890s, Ida B. Wells gathered evidence from newspapers, eyewitnesses, and public records.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice describes her methods.

questions.question:
Although the treaty's language was ____________, its meaning was clear to both sides: neither country would build new forts along the border.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: convoluted
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

“Although” contrasts complicated language with a clear meaning, so the wording was convoluted.

questions.question:
The study's authors were careful to ____________ their conclusions, noting that the results applied only to adults over sixty and might not hold for younger people.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: qualify
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Limiting a conclusion to one group is to qualify it.

questions.question:
The village's traditions have proved remarkably ____________: despite a century of rapid change, residents still celebrate the harvest with the same songs and dances their great-grandparents performed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: durable
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Traditions that survive a century of change are durable.

questions.question:
The chef's menu is deliberately ____________, offering only five dishes, each made from ingredients grown on the restaurant's own farm.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.correct: limited
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Offering only five dishes makes the menu limited.

questions.question:
The first vaccines against smallpox were made from material taken from cowpox sores. For more than a century, the method changed little. In the twentieth century, scientists learned to grow viruses in laboratory cultures, which made it possible to produce vaccines in large, consistent batches. These advances helped make possible a worldwide vaccination campaign, and in 1980 the World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It traces how methods of making a vaccine developed over time and connects them to an important outcome.
It compares smallpox with cowpox and explains why one disease is more dangerous.
It argues that the earliest vaccines were more effective than later ones.
It describes the work of the World Health Organization and lists its other campaigns.
questions.correct: It traces how methods of making a vaccine developed over time and connects them to an important outcome.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The text moves from early cowpox material, to laboratory production, to the eradication of smallpox.

questions.question:
Nearly every culture has stories about floods. Some researchers have suggested that a few of these stories may preserve memories of real events, such as rising sea levels at the end of the last ice age, when coastlines in many parts of the world moved inland. Others caution that floods are common enough that such stories need no single historical source.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes how sea levels are measured today.
It presents one possible explanation that the final sentence then qualifies.
It gives an example of a flood story from a particular culture.
It argues that all flood stories describe the same event.
questions.correct: It presents one possible explanation that the final sentence then qualifies.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The underlined sentence offers an explanation; the final sentence adds a note of caution.

questions.question:
Text 1

Many psychologists have argued that boredom is simply an unpleasant state that people should try to avoid, since it tends to lower mood and motivation.

Text 2

Psychologist Sandra Lindgren gave participants a dull task, such as copying numbers from a phone book, before asking them to think of creative uses for everyday objects. Participants who had done the dull task came up with more creative ideas than participants who had not. Lindgren suggests that boredom may encourage the mind to wander in useful ways.

Based on the texts, how would Lindgren (Text 2) most likely respond to the psychologists' view in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that boredom always lowers motivation and should be avoided
By suggesting that boredom may have benefits that the view does not consider
By arguing that copying numbers is an effective way to improve mood
By claiming that creative people are never bored
questions.correct: By suggesting that boredom may have benefits that the view does not consider
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Lindgren's finding that boredom boosted creativity points to an overlooked benefit.

questions.question:
Most bird species can fly, but flight is costly: it demands large amounts of energy and strong, lightweight bodies. On islands without predators, several bird species have lost the ability to fly over many generations. Without threats to escape from, these birds could survive by walking and running, and energy that would have been spent on flight could go to other needs, such as producing eggs.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Birds that live on islands are always larger than birds on the mainland.
Flightless birds can no longer produce eggs.
Because flight is costly, some birds on islands without predators have lost the ability to fly over time.
Predators on islands have caused many birds to lose the ability to fly.
questions.correct: Because flight is costly, some birds on islands without predators have lost the ability to fly over time.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The text explains the cost of flight and why the absence of predators allowed some birds to lose it.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Kwame has just moved into his first apartment.

The apartment was smaller than it had looked in the photos, and the kitchen faucet dripped no matter how hard he turned it. Kwame unpacked his boxes anyway, lining up his books on the windowsill because he had no shelves yet. That evening he cooked rice in the one pot he owned and ate it sitting on the floor, watching the lights come on across the street. It was not much, he thought. But it was his.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Kwame regrets moving out of his family's home.
Kwame plans to fix the faucet before unpacking his boxes.
Kwame dislikes his neighbors across the street.
Despite the apartment's flaws, Kwame takes satisfaction in having a place of his own.
questions.correct: Despite the apartment's flaws, Kwame takes satisfaction in having a place of his own.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

He notices the problems but ends feeling that the modest apartment is his own.

questions.question:
Economist Leila Farah claims that a city's new subway line raised the value of homes located near its stations.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' claim?
options: After the line opened, home prices rose faster near the new stations than in similar neighborhoods farther away, though prices in both areas had risen at the same rate before.
Many residents said that the subway line made commuting easier.
Home prices in the city as a whole rose during the decade.
The subway line was completed ahead of schedule.
questions.correct: After the line opened, home prices rose faster near the new stations than in similar neighborhoods farther away, though prices in both areas had risen at the same rate before.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Faster price growth only near the stations, after similar growth before, points to the subway as the cause.

questions.question:
A company let employees in three departments choose a hybrid schedule, working some days from home. A manager notes that the change seemed to raise satisfaction in two departments but not in Sales, where the percentage of employees reporting high satisfaction ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: was about the same under both schedules (58% and 57%).
was higher than in Engineering under both schedules.
questions.correct: was about the same under both schedules (58% and 57%).
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Sales shows almost no change, as the manager says.

questions.question:
A marine biologist compared two reefs, one protected from fishing and pollution and one not. Both were damaged by a heat wave in 2016. The biologist argues that protection helped the reef recover: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: coral cover on the protected reef rose from about 30% after the heat wave to about 44% by 2022, while cover on the unprotected reef stayed near 20%.
both reefs lost coral cover in 2016.
coral cover on the unprotected reef was about 40% in 2010.
coral cover on the unprotected reef rose to about 44% by 2022.
questions.correct: coral cover on the protected reef rose from about 30% after the heat wave to about 44% by 2022, while cover on the unprotected reef stayed near 20%.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice contrasts the protected reef's recovery with the unprotected reef's lack of recovery.

questions.question:
A nutrition student claims that the vitamin C in some fruits breaks down much faster during storage than in others. For example, after one week ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: strawberries had lost about a third of their vitamin C (60 to 41 mg), while oranges had lost very little (53 to 50 mg).
kiwis had the most vitamin C of the three fruits.
oranges had 50 mg of vitamin C per 100 g.
oranges had lost more vitamin C than strawberries.
questions.correct: strawberries had lost about a third of their vitamin C (60 to 41 mg), while oranges had lost very little (53 to 50 mg).
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice compares a large loss with a small one.

questions.question:
Some frogs in cold regions survive winter by freezing almost solid. Biologist Erik Holm found that as temperatures drop, these frogs fill their cells with high concentrations of glucose, a kind of sugar. In laboratory tests, frog tissues treated with similar amounts of glucose suffered much less damage from freezing than untreated tissues. These findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: frogs in cold regions eat more sugar in winter than in summer.
freezing makes frogs' cells produce less glucose.
frogs in warm regions cannot survive freezing because they lack cells.
glucose may help protect the frogs' cells from being damaged by freezing.
questions.correct: glucose may help protect the frogs' cells from being damaged by freezing.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Glucose reduced freezing damage in tissues, which points to its protective role.

questions.question:
Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in two different ____________ physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: sciences:
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A colon introduces the two sciences that explain “two different sciences.”

questions.question:
The flock of geese that rests on the lake each autumn ____________ grown larger every year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: has
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The subject is the singular “flock,” so the verb is has.

questions.question:
The old train station, which had been empty for ____________ was converted into a public market in 2019.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: decades,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The nonessential clause that begins with a comma after “station” must end with a comma.

questions.question:
Hoping to see the eclipse, ____________

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the town with clear skies was three hours away from the family.
the family drove three hours to a town with clear skies.
a three-hour drive took the family to a town with clear skies.
clear skies were found by the family in a town three hours away.
questions.correct: the family drove three hours to a town with clear skies.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The family did the hoping, so “the family” must follow the opening phrase.

questions.question:
The museum's newest exhibit features clothing from the 1920s, including beaded dresses, wool coats, and ____________ hats.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: felt
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

No punctuation belongs between the adjective “felt” and the noun “hats.”

questions.question:
The researchers found that students who read for pleasure scored higher on vocabulary tests than ____________

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the scores of students who did not.
that of students who did not.
questions.correct: students who did not.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Students are compared with other students; comparing students with “scores” or “that” is illogical.

questions.question:
If more people ____________ public transportation, the city's air would be cleaner.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.correct: used
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

A hypothetical present condition uses the past form used with “would” in the result.

questions.question:
The first draft of the report was nearly two hundred pages long. ____________ the final version, after careful editing, was just sixty pages.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: By contrast,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The short final version contrasts with the long first draft.

questions.question:
Many deep-sea fish are red. ____________ red light does not reach the deep ocean, these fish appear black and are nearly invisible.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: Because
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The fish look black for this reason: red light does not reach them.

questions.question:
The team spent a year studying how people use public benches. ____________ they found that benches facing a view were used twice as often as benches facing a wall.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.correct: Among other things,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The bench finding is one of several things the study found.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Dead Sea is a salt lake in the Middle East.
  • Its surface is about 430 meters below sea level, the lowest point on land on Earth.
  • Its water is about ten times saltier than ocean water.
  • Because the water is so salty, people float easily in it.

The student wants to explain why people float easily in the Dead Sea.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Dead Sea is a salt lake in the Middle East.
People float easily in the Dead Sea because its water is about ten times saltier than ocean water.
The surface of the Dead Sea is the lowest point on land on Earth.
The Dead Sea is about 430 meters below sea level.
questions.correct: People float easily in the Dead Sea because its water is about ten times saltier than ocean water.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only this choice gives the reason people float.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • A study tested whether doodling affects memory.
  • Participants listened to a dull phone message.
  • Half were asked to doodle while listening, and half were not.
  • The doodlers remembered about 29 percent more information from the message.

The student wants to present the study's result to readers who think doodling is a distraction.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In one study, participants listened to a dull phone message.
Half of the participants in one study were asked to doodle.
Although doodling is often seen as a distraction, participants in one study who doodled while listening to a message remembered about 29 percent more of it.
A study tested whether doodling affects memory.
questions.correct: Although doodling is often seen as a distraction, participants in one study who doodled while listening to a message remembered about 29 percent more of it.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice presents the result and addresses the view that doodling distracts.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Kazimir Malevich was a Russian painter born in 1879.
  • In 1915 he exhibited Black Square, a painting of a black square on a white background.
  • He called his style Suprematism.
  • Suprematism focused on simple geometric shapes rather than recognizable objects.

The student wants to describe the main idea of Suprematism.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Kazimir Malevich was a Russian painter born in 1879.
Kazimir Malevich called his style Suprematism.
Suprematism, the style developed by Kazimir Malevich, focused on simple geometric shapes rather than recognizable objects.
questions.correct: Suprematism, the style developed by Kazimir Malevich, focused on simple geometric shapes rather than recognizable objects.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Only this choice explains what Suprematism focused on.
